Youssef Chermiti class act as Portugal coach dedicates Euro qualification to injured Rangers man

Dakir Thanveer
Sun 4 October 2026 17:17, UK
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 0:45
Instaread

While Rangers continue to manage their attacking personnel amid injuries to key forwards like Lawrence Shankland, recognition from the international stage has highlighted the high regard in which Ibrox players are held.

Portugal Under-21s officially punched their ticket to next year’s UEFA European Championship finals, becoming only the third team to secure qualification behind Croatia and Norway, excluding hosts Serbia and Albania. The milestone was sealed following a commanding 4-0 victory over Gibraltar Under-21s on Wednesday, 30 September, with heavyweights England and France following suit.

However, the immediate aftermath of qualification belonged just as much to those absent from the pitch. Speaking directly to the press after the match, Portugal Under-21 head coach Luis Freire bypassed immediate tactical analysis to deliver a heartfelt tribute to players who had contributed to the journey before suffering setbacks.

Here is our list of Rangers’ most underrated players. Who is missing from this list for you and why?

Luis Freire dedicates Portugal Under-21s’ Euro qualification to Rangers star Youssef Chermiti

Freire specifically dedicated the achievement to Rangers striker Youssef Chermiti and Roger Fernandes, both of whom are battling serious injuries. The national team boss stated:

“I’m satisfied with the whole journey we had. I dedicate this qualification to Chermiti and Roger, who suffered serious injuries.”

Chermiti has played an important role in the qualification cycle, featuring in five qualifying fixtures for Portugal, including high-profile matches against Scotland and Azerbaijan earlier this year, and netting two goals along the way. Despite being sidelined during the final stretch due to a ligament injury suffered at Ibrox, his influence on the squad was clear enough to earn a public dedication from his manager.

It is worth noting that the former Everton centre-forward showed his support back by sharing a celebratory post on his Instagram stories last week.

MORE RANGERS STORIES

For Rangers, seeing a player of Chermiti’s profile valued so deeply on the international stage underscores the quality of talent currently housed at Ibrox. As the young striker works his way back to full fitness under Derek McInnes, this classy acknowledgement from the Portuguese camp serves as a reminder of the quality he will bring back to the Rangers frontline once he returns to action.

While there has been little update from Chermiti regarding his recovery, the striker silently showed he is focused on returning to action by stripping down his Instagram account to just a handful of posts of him in a Rangers kit.
